'''Kurt Leichtweiß''' (March 2, 1927 in [[Villingen-Schwenningen]] – June 23, 2013) was a [[mathematician]] specializing in [[convex geometry|convex]] and [[differential geometry]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.stuttgart-gedenkt.de/Traueranzeige/Kurt-Leichtweiss|title=obituary|date=June 29, 2013|publisher=[[Stuttgarter Zeitung]]|language=German|accessdate=30 June 2013}}</ref><ref name=Jackson/><ref name="UniStuttgart">{{cite web|url=https://www.uni-stuttgart.de/hkom/publikationen/uni-kurier/uk99/leute/lt105b.html|title=Kurt Leichtweiß 80|last=Hermann Hähl, Eberhard Teufel|date=2007-06-30|publisher=[[University of Stuttgart]]|language=German|accessdate=30 June 2013}}</ref>

In 1944, while still in high school Leichtweiß traveled to the [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics]] where his mathematical interests were encouraged.<ref name=Jackson>A. Jackson, [https://www.ams.org/notices/200007/fea-oberwolfach.pdf Oberwolfach, Yesterday and Today], ''[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society|AMS Notices]]'', Volume 47 (2000), Number 7, 758-765.</ref>  He studied at the [[University of Freiburg]] and the [[ETH Zurich]]. He was a student of [[Emanuel Sperner]] and [[Wilhelm Süss]].  He was then a lecturer in Freiburg and in 1963 became a professor at [[TU Berlin]]. From 1970 until his retirement in 1995, he was a professor at the [[University of Stuttgart]]. In 1995, he received the [[Wilhelm Blaschke#Legacy | Wilhelm Blaschke Medal]].

== Books ==

* (with [[Wilhelm Blaschke]]), ''Elementary Differential Geometry'', Springer, 1973.
* ''Affine geometry of convex bodies'', Wiley, 1998.
* ''Convex Geometry'', Springer, 1980.
* ''Analytic Geometry, First Course'', Teubner, 1972.
